voice.about: A clear, slow American male narrator. Speed below 1 slows the speech; the video stretches to fit.

scenes.show: This is Qalam: a free phonetic Arabic keyboard for Mac and Windows. You type Arabic the way you spell it.
scenes.say: This is Qalam: a free, phonetic Arabic keyboard for Mac and Windows. You type Arabic, the way you spell it.

scenes.show: After you install it, a short setup walks you through everything. It turns the keyboard on, then lets you pick your style, harakat and sukūn.
scenes.say: After you install it, a short setup walks you through everything. It turns the keyboard on, then lets you pick your style, harakaat, and sukoon.

scenes.show: To switch between English and Arabic, press Control-Space on a Mac, or Ctrl+Alt+A on Windows.
scenes.say: To switch between English and Arabic, press Control Space on a Mac, or Control, Alt, A, on Windows.

scenes.show: Type each letter, then its vowel. Sukūn and shadda appear by themselves: double a letter, and you get a shadda.
scenes.say: Type each letter, then its vowel. Sukoon and shadda appear by themselves. Double a letter, and you get a shadda.

scenes.show: Letters with no English match get simple keys. A lowercase e is ʿayn. Capital H, S, D, T and Z are the heavy letters. th, dh, kh and gh work as you'd expect. t' is tāʾ marbūṭa, and capital Y is alif maqṣūra.
scenes.say: Letters with no English match get simple keys. A lowercase E is ain. Capital H, S, D, T, and Z are the heavy letters. T H, D H, K H, and G H work as you would expect. T apostrophe is taa marbuta, and capital Y is alif maqsura.

scenes.show: For a hamza, type a capital A followed by its vowel. Qalam picks the right seat for you.
scenes.say: For a hamza, type a capital A, followed by its vowel. Qalam picks the right seat for you.

scenes.show: Long phrases work too: the article, sun letters, and in Qur'an style every mark of the mushaf.
scenes.say: Long phrases work too: the article, the sun letters, and in Quran style, every mark of the mushaf.

scenes.show: As you type, Qalam offers other spellings. Use the arrow keys to choose, and Space to put it in.
scenes.say: As you type, Qalam offers other spellings. Use the arrow keys to choose, and press space to put it in.

scenes.show: Sukūn is smart: it only appears where it's needed. Control-Shift-O on a Mac, or Ctrl+Alt+O on Windows, turns it off. The Harakat button removes every vowel mark.
scenes.say: Sukoon is smart: it only appears where it is needed. Control Shift O on a Mac, or Control Alt O on Windows, turns it off. The harakaat button removes every vowel mark.

scenes.show: Every shortcut can be changed in Settings, in case it clashes with another app.
scenes.say: Every shortcut can be changed in settings, in case it clashes with another app.

scenes.show: Where are the settings? On a Mac, click ق in the menu bar and open Qalam. On Windows, right-click the tray icon and choose Setup & settings.
scenes.say: Where are the settings? On a Mac, click the Qalam icon in the menu bar, and open Qalam. On Windows, right click the tray icon, and choose setup and settings.

scenes.show: In Settings you can choose the Arabic font and its size, including a Qur'an font.
scenes.say: In settings, you can choose the Arabic font and its size, including a Quran font.

scenes.show: Qalam keeps itself up to date. To check now: Settings → Updates on a Mac, or Check for updates in the Windows tray menu.
scenes.say: Qalam keeps itself up to date. To check now, open settings, then updates, on a Mac, or choose check for updates, in the Windows tray menu.

scenes.show: Qalam is free, works offline, and never sends your typing anywhere. Download it from our website.
scenes.say: Qalam is free, works offline, and never sends your typing anywhere. Download it from our website.
